oxygen.title: Make Enough Oxygen
oxygen.setup: Two ants, two helmets, melted ice, and a solar panel.
oxygen.how_html: Electricity splits the water. Tap the oxygen bubbles (O<sub>2</sub>) into the active tank. Let the hydrogen (H<sub>2</sub>) escape. Watch the counters — the cell makes two H<sub>2</sub> for every O<sub>2</sub>.

instructions.text: Electricity splits water into hydrogen and oxygen.
instructions.speak: Electricity splits water into hydrogen and oxygen.

instructions.text: Tap each oxygen bubble, labeled O<sub>2</sub>, to send it into the active helmet tank.
instructions.speak: Tap each oxygen bubble, labeled O two, to send it into the active helmet tank.

instructions.text: Let the hydrogen bubbles, labeled H<sub>2</sub>, rise and escape. Every O<sub>2</sub> made comes with exactly two H<sub>2</sub>.
instructions.speak: Let the hydrogen bubbles, labeled H two, rise and escape. Every O two made comes with exactly two H two.

fill_k.text: Fill Kepler’s tank. It needs six oxygen bubbles.
fill_k.speak: Fill Kepler's tank. It needs six oxygen bubbles.

fill_c.text: Fill Comet’s tank. It needs six oxygen bubbles.
fill_c.speak: Fill Comet's tank. It needs six oxygen bubbles.

quiz.text: For every O<sub>2</sub> kept, how many H<sub>2</sub> left the cell?
quiz.speak: For every O two kept, how many H two left the cell?

fill.text: Oxygen comes off the positive electrode on the right. Tap the O<sub>2</sub> bubbles, not the H<sub>2</sub>.
fill.speak: Oxygen comes off the positive electrode on the right. Tap the O two bubbles, not the H two.

fill.text: Fill the highlighted tank to six O<sub>2</sub>. All hydrogen vents on its own — watch H₂ escaped climb.
fill.speak: Fill the highlighted tank to six oxygen. All hydrogen vents on its own. Watch hydrogen escaped climb.

fill.text: Ignore H<sub>2</sub>. Keep tapping O<sub>2</sub> until the active tank bar is full.
fill.speak: Ignore H two. Keep tapping O two until the active tank bar is full.

quiz.text: Water is H<sub>2</sub>O. Count the atoms on each side of the split.
quiz.speak: Water is H two O. Count the atoms on each side of the split.

quiz.text: Two water molecules make two H<sub>2</sub> and one O<sub>2</sub>. Compare those numbers.
quiz.speak: Two water molecules make two H two and one O two. Compare those numbers.

quiz.text: The ratio is exact: two H<sub>2</sub> escaped for every one O<sub>2</sub> in the tank.
quiz.speak: The ratio is exact: two hydrogen escaped for every one oxygen in the tank.

intro.text: The cell splits water. Every O₂ made comes with exactly two H₂, which all vent (escape).
intro.speak: The cell splits water. Every O two made comes with exactly two H two, which all vent, or escape.

tank_ok.speak: Hydrogen made equals twice the oxygen made. All hydrogen escaped. Water is H two O.
tank_ok.text: H₂ made is twice O₂ made. All H₂ escaped.

tank_miss.speak: Some oxygen was missed. Hydrogen still escaped at two for every oxygen the cell made.
tank_miss.text: Some O₂ missed. H₂ still escaped at two per O₂ made.

done.text: Tanks full. Two H₂ escaped for every O₂ kept.
done.speak: Tanks full. Two H two escaped for every O two kept.

k_ok.text: Kepler’s tank: 12 H₂ made, 6 O₂ made. 6 O₂ in the tank. 12 H₂ escaped — twice the oxygen, because water is H₂O.
k_ok.speak: Kepler's tank: twelve hydrogen made, six oxygen made. Six oxygen in the tank. Twelve hydrogen escaped. Twice the oxygen, because water is H two O.

c_ok.text: Comet’s tank: 12 H₂ made, 6 O₂ made. 6 O₂ in the tank. 12 H₂ escaped — twice the oxygen, because water is H₂O.
c_ok.speak: Comet's tank: twelve hydrogen made, six oxygen made. Six oxygen in the tank. Twelve hydrogen escaped. Twice the oxygen, because water is H two O.

fan.title: Build the Fan
fan.setup: The colony’s first machine, built from scrap.
fan.how_html: Tap a part, or drag it onto the workbench, in build order: base, motor, blades, guard, cable last. Then switch it on and decide what it is for.

instructions.text: Assemble the fan from the parts on the tray.
instructions.speak: Assemble the fan from the parts on the tray.

instructions.text: Tap a part, or drag it onto the workbench, in order: base, then motor, blades, guard, and power cable last.
instructions.speak: Tap a part, or drag it onto the workbench, in order: base, then motor, blades, guard, and power cable last.

instructions.text: When it is built, switch it on and answer what it is actually for.
instructions.speak: When it is built, switch it on and answer what it is actually for.

build.text: Put the five parts on in the right order.
build.speak: Put the five parts on in the right order.

gauge.text: The fan is running. What has it done to the oxygen supply?
gauge.speak: The fan is running. What has it done to the oxygen supply?

job.text: What is the fan actually good for inside a sealed habitat?
job.speak: What is the fan actually good for inside a sealed habitat?

build.text: Start from the bottom. Something has to stand on the bench before anything else goes on.
build.speak: Start from the bottom. Something has to stand on the bench before anything else goes on.

build.text: Order: base plate, then motor, then blades, then the guard cage, then the power cable.
build.speak: Order: base plate, then motor, then blades, then the guard cage, then the power cable.

build.text: Put the base plate on first. Power cable is always last.
build.speak: Put the base plate on first. Power cable is always last.

gauge.text: Look at the oxygen gauge. Did the number change when the fan started?
gauge.speak: Look at the oxygen gauge. Did the number change when the fan started?

gauge.text: A fan moves gas that is already there. It does not run chemistry.
gauge.speak: A fan moves gas that is already there. It does not run chemistry.

gauge.text: The gauge is unchanged. The fan made no oxygen.
gauge.speak: The gauge is unchanged. The fan made no oxygen.

job.text: In a sealed room, exhaled carbon dioxide stays near you unless the air moves.
job.speak: In a sealed room, exhaled carbon dioxide stays near you unless the air moves.

job.text: Real habitats keep fans running to mix the air and push it through life support.
job.speak: Real habitats keep fans running to mix the air and push it through life support.

job.text: Its job is mixing the air inside the sealed habitat.
job.speak: Its job is mixing the air inside the sealed habitat.

build.text: Next part needed is shown below. Wrong parts shake off; nothing is lost.
build.speak: Next part needed is shown below. Wrong parts shake off; nothing is lost.

running.text: The fan is spinning. Dust moves. Check whether the oxygen gauge moved.
running.speak: The fan is spinning. Dust moves. Check whether the oxygen gauge moved.

done.text: The fan spins and mixes air. It does not make oxygen.
done.speak: The fan spins and mixes air. It does not make oxygen.

power.title: Power Budget
power.setup: Your solar panel makes only a little power. Choose what matters most, then deal with dust and night.
power.how_html: Put the devices in order, switch them on or off, clean the dust, then press Run it.

instructions.text: Use the up and down arrows, or drag a row, to put the devices in order. Then press Check order.
instructions.speak: Use the up and down arrows, or drag a row, to put the devices in order. Then press Check order.

instructions.text: Next, each device has a switch. Tap it to turn it on or off. The bar shows how much power you are using.
instructions.speak: Next, each device has a switch. Tap it to turn it on or off. The bar shows how much power you are using.

instructions.text: If dust covers the panel, tap Clean the panel. Then press Run it.
instructions.speak: If dust covers the panel, tap Clean the panel. Then press Run it.

rank.text: Put the five devices in order, from the one you need most to the one you need least.
rank.speak: Put the five devices in order, from the one you need most to the one you need least.

dust.text: Get your power back, and keep the air and the heater running.
dust.speak: Get your power back, and keep the air and the heater running.

night.text: At night you only have the battery. Make four units last until morning.
night.speak: At night you only have the battery. Make four units last until morning.

rank.text: Without air to breathe, you last only minutes. Air goes first.
rank.speak: Without air to breathe, you last only minutes. Air goes first.

rank.text: Mars nights often drop below minus 70 degrees Celsius. Heat comes next.
rank.speak: Mars nights often drop below minus 70 degrees Celsius. Heat comes next.

rank.text: From the top: air, heater, water-splitting rig, radio, lights.
rank.speak: From the top: air, heater, water-splitting rig, radio, lights.

dust.text: Sunlight has to reach the panel to make power. Wiping off the dust lets it in again.
dust.speak: Sunlight has to reach the panel to make power. Wiping off the dust lets it in again.

dust.text: If there still isn't enough power, turn off the least important devices first.
dust.speak: If there still isn't enough power, turn off the least important devices first.

dust.text: Clean the panel. Keep the air and the heater on. Turn off the other three. Press Run it.
dust.speak: Clean the panel. Keep the air and the heater on. Turn off the other three. Press Run it.

night.text: No sun means no new power. The battery is all you have.
night.speak: No sun means no new power. The battery is all you have.

night.text: Air and heat keep you alive until sunrise. Everything else can wait.
night.speak: Air and heat keep you alive until sunrise. Everything else can wait.

night.text: Turn on only the air and the heater. That uses four units. Press Run it.
night.speak: Turn on only the air and the heater. That uses four units. Press Run it.

rank.text: The list is mixed up. Move each device to where it belongs.
rank.speak: The list is mixed up. Move each device to where it belongs.

dust.text: Red dust has settled on the solar panel. Dust blocks sunlight, so the panel makes less power. Now the devices need more power than you have.
dust.speak: Red dust has settled on the solar panel. Dust blocks sunlight, so the panel makes less power. Now the devices need more power than you have.

night.text: The sun has set. The panel makes no power now, so only the battery is left.
night.speak: The sun has set. The panel makes no power now, so only the battery is left.

done.text: You kept the crew alive through dust and darkness. When power is short, the most important things come first.
done.speak: You kept the crew alive through dust and darkness. When power is short, the most important things come first.

ring.title: Ring Test
ring.setup: A way to ask a pressure shell if it is intact.
ring.how_html: Tap the habitat to ring it. Sealed rings clear and long; a crack is dull and short. Ring first, then choose. Outside, judge by length, not loudness.

instructions.text: First learn two sounds: sealed rings clear and long; cracked is dull and short.
instructions.speak: First learn two sounds. Sealed rings clear and long. Cracked is dull and short.

instructions.text: Watch the ripple bar under each panel. Long means sealed. Short means a crack.
instructions.speak: Watch the ripple bar under each panel. Long means sealed. Short means a crack.

instructions.text: Then try it yourself. Replay Sealed and Cracked anytime from the buttons at the top.
instructions.speak: Then try it yourself. Replay Sealed and Cracked anytime from the buttons at the top.

intro.text: Listen to a sealed panel, then a cracked one.
intro.speak: Listen to a sealed panel, then a cracked one.

r1.text: Two panels. Ring both, then tap which one is cracked.
r1.speak: Two panels. Ring both, then tap which one is cracked.

r2.text: One shell sounds cracked. Find which of its three panels is the dull one, then patch it.
r2.speak: One shell sounds cracked. Find which of its three panels is the dull one, then patch it.

r3.text: Outside in thin air. Both are quieter. Pick the sealed shell by how long it rings.
r3.speak: Outside in thin air. Both are quieter. Pick the sealed shell by how long it rings.

intro.text: Tap Sealed and watch the ripple bar fill almost all the way.
intro.speak: Tap Sealed and watch the ripple bar fill almost all the way.

intro.text: Tap Cracked. The bar stops short and the sound is dull.
intro.speak: Tap Cracked. The bar stops short and the sound is dull.

intro.text: When you know both sounds, press Start the test.
intro.speak: When you know both sounds, press Start the test.

r1.text: Ring both panels. Use Sealed and Cracked at the top if you forget the sounds.
r1.speak: Ring both panels. Use Sealed and Cracked at the top if you forget the sounds.

r1.text: The cracked panel’s ripple bar is short. The sealed one’s bar is long.
r1.speak: The cracked panel's ripple bar is short. The sealed one's bar is long.

r1.text: Tap the choice under the panel whose bar died quickly.
r1.speak: Tap the choice under the panel whose bar died quickly.

r2.text: Ring the shell once. A short, rattly ring means a leak somewhere on it.
r2.speak: Ring the shell once. A short, rattly ring means a leak somewhere on it.

r2.text: Tap each panel segment. The cracked one dies quickly.
r2.speak: Tap each panel segment. The cracked one dies quickly.

r2.text: Patch the panel whose ring is shortest.
r2.speak: Patch the panel whose ring is shortest.

r3.text: Ring both shells. Outside, both sound quiet.
r3.speak: Ring both shells. Outside, both sound quiet.

r3.text: Compare how long each ripple bar runs, not how loud they are.
r3.speak: Compare how long each ripple bar runs, not how loud they are.

r3.text: Pick the shell whose bar lasts longer.
r3.speak: Pick the shell whose bar lasts longer.

intro.text: Tap each panel to hear it. Watch how long the bar stays lit.
intro.speak: Tap each panel to hear it. Watch how long the bar stays lit.

practice.text: You have heard both sounds. Use Start the test when you are ready.
practice.speak: You have heard both sounds. Use Start the test when you are ready.

listen.text: Length of the ring is the clue. Long and clear means sealed. Short and dull means a crack.
listen.speak: Length of the ring is the clue. Long and clear means sealed. Short and dull means a crack.

done.text: Seal holds. Quiet is not the same as cracked — length still tells the truth.
done.speak: Seal holds. Quiet is not the same as cracked. Length still tells the truth.

intro_lines.text: A crack lets the habitat’s air leak out. Cracked metal can’t ring for long, so a dull sound means look closer.
intro_lines.speak: A crack lets the habitat's air leak out. Cracked metal can't ring for long, so a dull sound means look closer.

intro_lines.text: Engineers use a tap test on aircraft and spacecraft to find hidden cracks.
intro_lines.speak: Engineers use a tap test on aircraft and spacecraft to find hidden cracks.

route.title: Route the Habitat
route.setup: Ice, power, and scrap. The pieces are here; the links are not.
route.how_html: Tap stations in order, or drag between them. Round one: ice → melter → splitter → O₂ tank → habitat. Then power and vent lines. Then put the fan in the habitat.

instructions.text: Connect the stations in order. Tap one station, then the next, or drag between them.
instructions.speak: Connect the stations in order. Tap one station, then the next, or drag between them.

instructions.text: Round one lays the air path: ice, melter, splitter, oxygen tank, habitat.
instructions.speak: Round one lays the air path: ice, melter, splitter, oxygen tank, habitat.

instructions.text: Round two adds power to the melter and splitter, and a vent for hydrogen. Round three places the fan inside the habitat, then ring-tests the seal.
instructions.speak: Round two adds power to the melter and splitter, and a vent for hydrogen. Round three places the fan inside the habitat, then ring-tests the seal.

air.text: Lay pipe from the ice to the habitat, one station at a time.
air.speak: Lay pipe from the ice to the habitat, one station at a time.

power.text: Connect power to the melter and splitter, and vent the hydrogen.
power.speak: Connect power to the melter and splitter, and vent the hydrogen.

seal.text: Put the fan inside the habitat, then ring-test the seal.
seal.speak: Put the fan inside the habitat, then ring-test the seal.

air.text: Start at the glowing ice deposit and move one step at a time toward the habitat.
air.speak: Start at the glowing ice deposit and move one step at a time toward the habitat.

air.text: Ice must melt before it can be split. Store oxygen in a tank before it enters the habitat.
air.speak: Ice must melt before it can be split. Store oxygen in a tank before it enters the habitat.

air.text: Connect: Ice deposit, Melter, Splitter, O₂ tank, Habitat.
air.speak: Connect: Ice deposit, Melter, Splitter, O two tank, Habitat.

power.text: The solar panel must feed the machines that use electricity: the melter and the splitter.
power.speak: The solar panel must feed the machines that use electricity: the melter and the splitter.

power.text: Hydrogen from the splitter needs its own way out, not into the habitat.
power.speak: Hydrogen from the splitter needs its own way out, not into the habitat.

power.text: Make three links: panel to melter, panel to splitter, and splitter to H₂ vent.
power.speak: Make three links: panel to melter, panel to splitter, and splitter to H two vent.

seal.text: The fan mixes air. It belongs where people breathe.
seal.speak: The fan mixes air. It belongs where people breathe.

seal.text: Connect the fan to the habitat, then use the ring button.
seal.speak: Connect the fan to the habitat, then use the ring button.

seal.text: Link Fan to Habitat, then tap Ring the habitat.
seal.speak: Link Fan to Habitat, then tap Ring the habitat.

air.text: Follow the glowing station. Each good link lights the next step on the air path.
air.speak: Follow the glowing station. Each good link lights the next step on the air path.

power.text: Three connections left: panel power and a hydrogen vent.
power.speak: Three connections left: panel power and a hydrogen vent.

seal.text: Place the fan inside, then ring-test the finished shell.
seal.speak: Place the fan inside, then ring-test the finished shell.

done.text: Air path, power, vent, fan, and a clear ring. The habitat holds.
done.speak: Air path, power, vent, fan, and a clear ring. The habitat holds.
